Sort tone labels for display

Source: R/tones.R
sort_tones.Rd

Returns the distinct tone labels in x in the order to show them, for example in a plot legend, facets or a table. The traditional Chinese tone category names come first, in the traditional order: ping, shang, qu, ru (level, rising, departing, entering), with yin before yang within each. So Mandarin's yinping, yangping, shangsheng and qusheng, written in Chinese characters, keep that order instead of the reverse order that sorting by code point gives. Other labels, such as T1, tone2 or 55, follow in natural order.

Usage

sort_tones(x, natural = TRUE)

Arguments

x

A vector of tone labels. A factor's levels are returned as they are, so a factor sets its own order.

natural

If TRUE (default), labels that are not Chinese tone names are in natural order; if FALSE, in the order factor() gives them.

Value

A character vector of the distinct non-missing labels of x, or, for a factor, its levels.

Details

A Chinese tone name is a category character (ping, shang, qu or ru), optionally preceded by yin or yang and followed by sheng or diao, in simplified or traditional characters (the yinping of simplified and of traditional characters both count). The entering tone may also be zhong, shangyin or xiayin (as in Cantonese), placed between yin and yang. Within a category, a name without yin or yang comes first. Space around a label is ignored when matching. Anything else, such as the neutral tone qingsheng or tone numbers written in Chinese, sorts with the other labels.

Natural order compares runs of digits as numbers, ignoring case, so T2 comes before T10. With natural = FALSE the other labels are in the order factor() gives them: alphabetical in the current locale, or numeric for a numeric x.

Examples

sort_tones(c("T10", "T2", "T1"))
#> [1] "T1"  "T2"  "T10"

# Mandarin tone names: yinping, yangping, shangsheng, qusheng
x <- c("\u4e0a\u58f0", "\u53bb\u58f0", "\u9633\u5e73", "\u9634\u5e73")
sort(x)          # locale order, often by code point
#> [1] "上声" "去声" "阳平" "阴平"
sort_tones(x)
#> [1] "阴平" "阳平" "上声" "去声"

# Use the result as factor levels, e.g. for a ggplot2 legend
factor(x, levels = sort_tones(x))
#> [1] 上声 去声 阳平 阴平
#> Levels: 阴平 阳平 上声 去声
